title: Weak relative Noether normalization
statement: Let $R$ and $A$ be commutative rings and let $h:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be the induced morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $h$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $N\ge0$ be an integer and suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $h$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Then there exist an integer $d$ with $0\le d\le N$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[T_1,\ldots,T_d]\to A$ from the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] such that the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R[T_1,\ldots,T_d])$ is quasi-finite (of finite type with finite discrete fibres, [pqf-def-quasifinite]).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 0GTG (lemma-weak-relative-noether-normalization): a finite type ring map with fibre dimensions bounded by d admits a quasi-finite map from a polynomial ring in d variables over the base.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] on the given affine morphism to see that $A$ is a finite type $R$-algebra. We will prove the stronger conclusion with exactly $N$ coordinates. Throughout, if $C$ is generated by finitely many elements over $B$, then $\operatorname{Spec}(C)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ is of finite type: the global affine pair gives local finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], and the morphism is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. If $B$ is enlarged to a polynomial ring mapping to $C$, the same generators still generate $C$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies fibres with spectra of the tensor products with residue fields. These observations apply to every ring map constructed below.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, initial finite-type affine setup and affine interpretation throughout

proof.text: First reduce to finite presentation. Write $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/J$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Index the finitely generated subideals $J_\lambda\subseteq J$ by inclusion; this is a small nonempty directed poset because sums give upper bounds. Put $A_\lambda=R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/J_\lambda$. These algebras are finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], their transition maps are surjective, and their colimit is $A$: every polynomial relation in $J$ belongs to a finitely generated subideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound] with constant base $R$ and bound $N$ to obtain a stage whose fibres all have dimension at most $N$. A quasi-finite map $R[T_1,\ldots,T_N]\to A_\lambda$, if obtained, gives one to $A$ by composition with the quotient: the same algebra generators descend, and for each target prime the primes of the quotient fibre identify with the subset of primes of the old fibre containing the quotient ideal. The old fibres are affine and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and quasi-finiteness makes all their points isolated; the singleton open cover therefore has a finite subcover. Thus each new fibre is a subspace of a finite discrete fibre, hence finite and discrete. This is quasi-finiteness [pqf-def-quasifinite]. It suffices to prove the claim for finitely presented algebras.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, first proof paragraph; Tag 05M5, limits.tex label lemma-limit-dimension

proof.text: For finitely presented $R\to A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation] with the zero module (which is finitely presented). After a common universe enlargement, its indexing set is small. It gives a directed system $R_\lambda\to A_\lambda$ with colimit $R\to A$, each $R_\lambda$ finite type over $\mathbf Z$, each $A_\lambda$ finite type over $R_\lambda$, and comparison and limit base-change isomorphisms. In particular $A_\lambda$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$: adjoin its finitely many algebra generators to the finitely many ring generators of $R_\lambda$. The comparison maps are isomorphisms, hence surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound] gives a stage with all fibre dimensions at most $N$. A quasi-finite map $R_\lambda[T_1,\ldots,T_N]\to A_\lambda$ is locally quasi-finite by the forward direction of [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc]. It base changes to the required map over $R$: finite type is preserved by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and local quasi-finiteness by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change]. A finite type morphism is quasi-compact, so the converse direction of [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] shows the result is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. The target tensor product is $R[T_1,\ldots,T_N]$: the isomorphism sends $p\otimes r$ to $r p$ with coefficients mapped to $R$; its inverse sends $r$ to $1\otimes r$ and each variable to $T_i\otimes1$. The source tensor product is $A$ by the cited limit theorem and the affine fibre-product formula. We are reduced to $R,A$ finite type over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, second proof paragraph; use 00R1 and 05M5 (the bound-only assertion needs no pure-relative-dimension hypothesis)

proof.text: For rings $R,A$ finite type over $\mathbf Z$, induct on the bound $N$, simultaneously for all such ring maps. When $N=0$, each fibre is a finite-type scheme over its residue field by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. It is finite and discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian]. The original finite-type morphism is therefore quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], giving the zero-variable map $R\to A$. Empty fibres cause no exception. For $N>0$, assume the result for $N-1$ over every base of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. We will construct $c\in A$ such that all fibres of $R[t]\to A$, $t\mapsto c$, have dimension at most $N-1$, before applying that outer induction hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, third proof paragraph (induction on the fibre bound)

proof.text: For this coordinate construction with fixed $N>0$, use a second induction on $\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. This is a finite integer when $R\ne0$: write $R$ as a quotient of $\mathbf Z[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal by the division algorithm (choose its least positive member if nonzero); hence $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian, since the union of an ascending chain of ideals is generated by one element already in a stage. Its dimension is at most one by [lem-trf-principal-ideal-ring-dimension-bound], and the polynomial dimension formula [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] bounds the polynomial ring dimension by $m+1$. Inverse images lift any strict chain of primes of a quotient to a strict chain in that polynomial ring, so $\dim R\le m+1$. Treat $R=0$ separately: then its unital algebra $A$ is zero and $c=0$ works. If $A=0$ the same choice works over any $R$. The inner induction hypothesis is the coordinate construction for every finite-type $\mathbf Z$-base of strictly smaller dimension, with the same bound $N$.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, fourth proof paragraph: justify finite base dimension and state the inner induction precisely

proof.text: For nonzero $R$ and $A$, apply [lem-trf-generic-principal-coordinate-dimension-drop] with $S=A$ and $d=N$. Obtain $a_0\in A$ and $f\in R$ avoiding every minimal prime of $R$, such that $R_f[t]\to A_f$, $t\mapsto a_0$, has all fibres of dimension at most $N-1$. Replace $a_0$ by $a=f a_0\in fA$. This keeps the bound over $R_f$: the new map is the old map precomposed with the automorphism of $R_f[t]$ sending $t$ to $f t$, whose inverse sends $t$ to $f^{-1}t$. This only relabels the target points and identifies the corresponding fibres. Inverting $f$ has the meaning of [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0GTG, generic-point and shrinking paragraphs, through the replacement a by fa

proof.text: The quotient $R/fR$ has strictly smaller dimension than $R$, unless it is zero (the empty-base case already handled). Indeed lift a prime chain of $R/fR$ to a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_s$ in $R$, every member containing $f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p_0$. Since $f\notin\mathfrak q$, this inclusion is strict; adjoining $\mathfrak q$ gives a chain one longer, so $s+1\le\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Both $R/fR$ and $A/fA$ remain finite type over $\mathbf Z$, by taking images of generators. Their fibres are the original fibres over primes containing $f$: for such a prime $\mathfrak p$, $(A/fA)\otimes_{R/fR}\kappa(\mathfrak p/fR)\cong A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, via the maps induced by $\bar a\otimes u\mapsto a\otimes u$ and its inverse. Thus their fibre dimensions are still at most $N$. The inner induction gives $\bar b\in A/fA$ for which $(R/fR)[t]\to A/fA$, $t\mapsto\bar b$, has all fibre dimensions at most $N-1$. If the quotient is zero take $\bar b=0$. Choose a lift $b\in A$.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, final paragraph: justify dimension decrease and apply inner induction to the closed complement

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-power-perturbation-fibre-dimension] to the finite type map $R_f\to A_f$, the elements $a,b$, and the nonnegative bound $N-1$. Choose $n\ge\max(1,n_0)$ and set $c=a^n+b\in A$. Over $R_f$ the map $t\mapsto c$ has fibre dimension at most $N-1$. Modulo $f$, $a\in fA$ and $n>0$ imply $\bar c=\bar b$, so the same bound holds on the quotient. To check every fibre of $R[t]\to A$, let $Q\subset R[t]$ be prime and put $\mathfrak p=Q\cap R$. If $f\notin\mathfrak p$, localizing at $f$ does not change this fibre: $A_f\otimes_{R_f[t]}\kappa(QR_f[t])\cong A\otimes_{R[t]}\kappa(Q)$, since $f$ is invertible in this field. If $f\in\mathfrak p$, the fibre is $(A/fA)\otimes_{(R/fR)[t]}\kappa(Q/fR[t])$, because $f$ acts by zero. The residue fields here are the original $\kappa(Q)$, being fraction fields of the same quotient domain, and the tensor identifications send the image of $x\otimes u$ to $x\otimes u$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Every prime is in exactly one case, proving the coordinate construction and closing the inner induction.

source.place: Tag 0GTG, final three sentences; Tag 0GTF, label lemma-sum-is-ok, applied over R_f with bound N-1

proof.text: The ring $R[t]$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$ (adjoin $t$ to generators of $R$), and $A$ is finite type over $R[t]$ with $t\mapsto c$ (retain its generators over $R$) [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply the outer induction hypothesis with bound $N-1$ to this new map. It gives a quasi-finite map $(R[t])[u_1,\ldots,u_{N-1}]\to A$. Identify its source with $R[T_1,\ldots,T_N]$ by $T_1=t$ and $T_{i+1}=u_i$; the inverse is the same substitution in reverse. This is the desired map with exactly $N$ coordinates, closing the outer induction. Steps 2 and 3 then give that map for the original $R$ and $A$. Take $d=N$, so $0\le d\le N$.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks 0GTG by its two limit reductions, outer induction on N, and inner induction on the finite base dimension. Reused the existing affine 05M5 and 00R1 nodes. Added only the dense-principal-open coordinate lemma and the independent 0GTF power-perturbation lemma; both are statement-only and searched. Wrote the quotient chain bound, scaling automorphism and fibre computations for a^n+b explicitly, including zero rings and empty fibres. The original statement is unchanged; the proof constructs exactly N variables. Added the existing polynomial-ring definition reference to the statement, with no mathematical change.
split_report.blueprint: The ancestor lem-trf-local-term-locality has no normalization sentence. This realizes its recorded via chain, specifically the affine normalization core used in Step 2 of lem-trf-local-quasi-finite-projection (a tool for the bounded-dimension local model). The proof follows Stacks 0GTG without changing the unit route.

tool_uses.why: The generic affine limit-dimension tool (05M5) supplies both finite-presentation approximation and descent of the upper bound; the trace unit has no replacement for this limit theorem.
The generic finite-presentation model theorem (00R1), with zero module, supplies finite-type integer models and their base-change isomorphisms.
Generic scheme permanence of local quasi-finiteness is used only to base change the normalization map from its finite-type integer model.

Generic equivalence quasi-finite = locally quasi-finite + quasi-compact, needed in step 3 to pass between the isolated-point definition and the local quasi-finiteness that base change preserves; the trace unit has no node for it.

The item statement is correct and unchanged apart from the added polynomial-ring citation. The N-variable proof implies the stated 0<=d<=N, and the A=0 and R=0 cases work. Steps 1-9 follow 0GTG. Step 3 uses 05M5 instead of 0EY2, which is valid because isomorphisms are closed immersions. The rescaling t->ft, the strict drop dim R/fR < dim R via a minimal prime avoiding f, and the f-in/f-not-in fibre identifications in step 8 all check. New node generic-principal-coordinate-dimension-drop is exactly the 0GTG intermediate result through V=D(f) by prime avoidance. It is true when d is only an upper bound, I tested it on k[s,x]/(sx), non-reduced and reducible bases and dim R=0, and it does not restate a clause of the item. New node power-perturbation-fibre-dimension is 0GTF with identical hypotheses, and its threshold is needed: x^n-x^m fails at n=m. Duplicate search by 0GTG/0GTF/0GTE/sum-is-ok/Noether normalization and dense/principal-open fibre wording found nothing; candidates read are listed in review.md. One fault, fixed (C1/C4): step 3 moved between quasi-finite (the isolated-point definition) and locally quasi-finite, citing only pqf-def-quasifinite. The fix adds the existing node pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc to the step text, uses, proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses. It does not depend on the item, so no cycle. lean.statement: theorem weakRelativeNoetherNormalization {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (hft : LocallyOfFiniteType (Scheme.Spec.map (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))) ∧ QuasiCompact (Scheme.Spec.map (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A))))) (N : ℕ) (hN : ∀ y, topologicalKrullDim ((Scheme.Spec.map (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))).fiber y) ≤ (N : ℕ∞)) : ∃ d : ℕ, 0 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ N ∧ ∃ g : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] A, Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFinite (Scheme.Spec.map (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.ofHom g.toRingHom)))
